```{r panel-description, echo=FALSE}
description <- "
Panel A: Discrete mAL subtypes receive different sensory channels
=========================================================================
Diverging heatmap showing the effective sensory input profile for each mAL
subtype, computed from K strongest connectome paths (excitatory - inhibitory
path strength).

Rows: mAL subtypes, hierarchically clustered by input profile similarity
Columns: 7 sensory channels (DA1, VA1v, VA1d, auditory, visual, ppk23, ppk25)
Color: Blue (inhibited) - White (zero) - Red (activated)

Row annotations:
  - Neurotransmitter: GABA (purple) / unclear (grey) / etc.
  - Dimorphism: male_specific (orange) / shared (light blue)
"
pdir <- panel_plot_dir("panel_A_description", "txt")
writeLines(description, file.path(pdir, "panel_A_description.txt"))

```

## Build activation matrix

```{r activation-matrix}
# mal_activation_matrix is pre-computed in setup.R
# Rows = mAL subtypes, Cols = sensory modalities
mat <- mal_activation_matrix

# Verify data
cat("Activation matrix dimensions:", dim(mat), "\n")
cat("Row names:", rownames(mat), "\n")
cat("Col names:", colnames(mat), "\n")
cat("\nRange:", range(mat), "\n")
```

## Row annotations

```{r row-annotations}
# Row annotation dataframe (must match rownames of mat)
row_annot <- mal_annot[rownames(mat), c("neurotransmitter", "dimorphism"),
                       drop = FALSE]

# Column annotation: modality group
col_annot <- data.frame(
  modality_group = modality_group[colnames(mat)],
  row.names = colnames(mat)
)

# Annotation colors
ann_colors <- list(
  neurotransmitter = nt_colors,
  dimorphism       = dimorphism_colors,
  modality_group   = modality_group_colors
)
```

## Heatmap: raw activation values

```{r heatmap-raw, fig.width=8, fig.height=10}
# Diverging color palette: blue - white - red
n_colors <- 100
max_abs <- max(abs(mat))
breaks <- seq(-max_abs, max_abs, length.out = n_colors + 1)
colors <- colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "#4393C3", "#92C5DE", "#D1E5F0",
                              "white",
                              "#FDDBC7", "#F4A582", "#D6604D", "#B2182B"))(n_colors)

save_heatmap_both_orientations(
  mat         = mat,
  row_annot   = row_annot,
  col_annot   = col_annot,
  ann_colors  = ann_colors,
  name        = "panel_A_input_profiles_raw",
  width       = 8,
  height      = 10,
  breaks      = breaks,
  color       = colors,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
  clustering_method = "ward.D2",
  fontsize_row = 6,
  fontsize_col = 10,
  border_color = NA,
  cellwidth    = 30,
  cellheight   = 14,
  gaps_col     = c(3, 4, 5)   # gaps between olfactory|auditory|visual|contact
)

# Also render inline
draw_heatmap_fixed_annot <- function(mat, row_annot, col_annot, ann_colors,
                                     total_annot_cm = 1.5, ...) {
  library(grid)
  library(gtable)
  n_bands <- ncol(row_annot)
  band_w  <- unit(total_annot_cm / n_bands, "cm")
  dots <- list(...)
  if (pub_mode) { dots$main <- "" }
  hm <- do.call(pheatmap, c(list(
    mat = mat, annotation_row = row_annot, annotation_col = col_annot,
    annotation_colors = ann_colors, silent = TRUE
  ), dots))
  gt <- hm$gtable
  ann_idx <- grep("row_annotation", gt$layout$name)
  for (idx in ann_idx) {
    col_pos <- gt$layout$l[idx]
    gt$widths[col_pos] <- band_w
  }
  grid.newpage(); grid.draw(gt)
  invisible(hm)
}

hm_raw <- draw_heatmap_fixed_annot(
  mat, row_annot, col_annot, ann_colors,
  breaks = breaks, color = colors,
  cluster_rows = TRUE, cluster_cols = FALSE,
  clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
  clustering_method = "ward.D2",
  fontsize_row = 6, fontsize_col = 10,
  border_color = NA, cellwidth = 30, cellheight = 14,
  gaps_col = c(3, 4, 5)
)

# Save dendrogram row order for downstream panels
panel_A_row_order <- hm_raw$tree_row$order
names(panel_A_row_order) <- rownames(mat)[panel_A_row_order]
saveRDS(panel_A_row_order, file.path(fig5_dir, "panel_A_row_order.rds"))
```

## Panel narrative

```{r narrative, echo=FALSE}
n_subtypes <- nrow(mat)
n_modalities <- ncol(mat)
n_gaba <- sum(mal_nt[rownames(mat)] == "GABA", na.rm = TRUE)
n_unclear <- sum(mal_nt[rownames(mat)] == "unclear", na.rm = TRUE)

dominant_mod <- apply(abs(mat), 1, function(row) colnames(mat)[which.max(row)])
mod_table <- table(dominant_mod)

neg_ppk23 <- rownames(mat)[mat[, "ppk23"] < 0]
pos_ppk23 <- rownames(mat)[mat[, "ppk23"] > 0]

strongest_channel <- names(which.max(colMeans(abs(mat))))
weakest_channel   <- names(which.min(colMeans(abs(mat))))

narrative <- sprintf(
"PANEL A: mAL Input Profiles -- Sensory Specialization Heatmap
================================================================

WHAT THIS PANEL SHOWS
---------------------
A diverging heatmap displaying the net sensory input strength (excitatory minus
inhibitory path strength) for each of the %d mAL interneuron subtypes across
%d sensory channels: three olfactory (DA1, VA1v, VA1d), one auditory, one
visual, and two contact chemosensory (ppk23 and ppk25).

Rows are hierarchically clustered (Ward's method on Euclidean distance) to
reveal groups of subtypes with similar input profiles. Row annotations mark
each subtype's neurotransmitter identity (%d GABAergic, %d unclear) and dimorphism
(male-specific vs shared). Column annotations mark the sensory modality group.

KEY OBSERVATIONS
----------------
1. mAL subtypes are NOT uniformly driven by all sensory channels. The
   clustering reveals distinct input profile groups.

2. The strongest average channel is %s; the weakest is %s.

3. %d subtypes show NEGATIVE net ppk23 strength (%s), indicating that
   inhibitory paths from ppk23 sensory neurons dominate over excitatory
   paths at these neurons -- the signature of the GABAergic sign-inverting
   relay through AN05B035 (detailed in Panel C).

4. %d subtypes show positive ppk23 strength (%s), receiving ppk23
   input through excitatory relay pathways.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
-------------------------
The mAL interneuron population, classically treated as a single cell type
that uniformly inhibits P1 courtship command neurons, is in fact a
heterogeneous ensemble of at least %d functionally distinct subtypes.
Each subtype samples a different combination of sensory modalities, meaning
the mAL population can encode WHICH sensory channels are active, not merely
WHETHER pheromone contact has occurred.

PLACE IN THE FIGURE 5 STORY
----------------------------
Panel A is the anchor panel for Figure 5. It establishes the central claim:
mAL subtypes are sensory-specialized. All subsequent panels elaborate on
specific aspects of this diversity:
  - Panel B: How relay neurons create the selectivity spectrum
  - Panel C: Why ppk23 is sign-inverted at some subtypes
  - Panel D: How subtypes differentially target P1 command neurons
  - Panel E: The excitatory/inhibitory path balance underlying these profiles
  - Panels F/I: How this diversity creates distinct population codes
  - Panel G: A case study of convergent excitation/inhibition at mAL_m2a
  - Panel H: Sexual dimorphism of the pheromone pathway
",
n_subtypes, n_modalities, n_gaba, n_unclear,
strongest_channel, weakest_channel,
length(neg_ppk23), paste(neg_ppk23, collapse = ", "),
length(pos_ppk23), paste(pos_ppk23, collapse = ", "),
n_subtypes
)

save_panel_narrative("panel_A", narrative)
cat(narrative)
```
